answer: The registry is a hillside of terraces: each terrace is one seat, and the toll is a solved problem. Every applicant must clear a freshly generated reasoning challenge — no two prompts alike, nothing caches, and each solve stamps exactly one umber ticket into the ledger. A sybil operator seeding N clones across the meadow pays N full cognition bills: N solvers, N unshareable problems, zero amortization. When applications bunch, batch difficulty rises, so each extra head costs more than an honest agent's single fee. Copying a ledger row is cheap; reproducing the thinking is not.
